_dl_cache_note: WHY THIS BUILD'S CEILING JUMPED +34.8% (159939 -> 215663) WHILE THE REAL
PER-FRAME WORK WENT DOWN. The whole increase is workstream A's dl_cache
line fill (ISR loop 2): 24 iterations of 4 SDRAM words, and the longest-path
model is free to assume EVERY tap lane fills on the SAME frame. It cannot:
dc_stencil refuses a refill until that lane's line is DC_MIN_SPAN = 32
frames old, so across a 16-frame block at most 16/32 = 0.5 lane-fills can
occur, against the 8-per-frame the model prices. Measured over the 200k-frame
golden scenario the cache issues 0.66 SDRAM words per tap read against 4.00
for the direct path -- i.e. it REDUCES real FMC traffic ~6x while raising the
modelled ceiling ~35%.
Quantified by building both ways (2026-08-23): with DL_CACHE_ENABLE=0 the
combined A+B image's ceiling is 153351, which is 4.1% BELOW the pre-merge
baseline -- so every other part of this integration lowers the modelled
worst case, and the cache alone accounts for all of the growth.
The tool has no way to express a rate limit, and inventing one would make it
trust a claim instead of checking one. The baseline is therefore recorded
WITH the pessimism in it: it still detects regressions (it is a ratio between
builds), it just must not be read as a load prediction. The number that
settles the cache is g_isr_pk on the unit with DL_CACHE_ENABLE 1 vs 0 --
the bench gate workstream A already specified.
_readme: Manifest for tools/wcet.py — the machine-checkable half of budget
contract clause C-3. Every entry here is a CLAIM about the code that CI
re-checks on every build. `loops` is the number of cycles (strongly
connected components, reducible or not) the compiler emitted for that
function: it is deliberately brittle, because a change to it means the
loop structure of the audio ISR changed and a human must look. Bounds are
read out of each loop's own `cmp rN,#imm` exit test where one exists (see
infer_bound); `default_bound` covers the rest and needs the justification
in `why`. A loop with no edge leaving its body is rejected outright.
_sdram_note: These are the out-of-line readers of the external delay buffer; their
loads are priced at SDRAM_LOAD rather than SRAM. SDRAM traffic that the
compiler INLINED into bsp_audio_isr (dl_write, pt_read/pt_write, the
overdub read-modify-write) is still priced as SRAM — the model cannot
tell which pointer an inlined load followed. That underestimate is one of
the things the calibration ratio K absorbs; it is also why the ratio
between builds, not the absolute ceiling, is the regression signal.

_note: K = measured worst-case cycles / modelled ceiling, recorded with
--calibrate <isr_pk>. The ceiling assumes the most expensive branch
everywhere at once, so it is larger than any single real path; K says
by how much, for a build whose real load is known.
PROVENANCE of this value: the measurement is the lead's, isr_pk 4104 =
117% of budget in TIME/RECIRC with a loop playing, taken on the image
BEFORE workstream B's changes; the ceiling it is divided by is the
image AFTER them, because that is the one this tool can disassemble.
The two differ, so treat this K as an anchor of the right order and
re-record it next time the unit is on the bench: build, flash, reset
g_isr_pk, run the WCC-TIME programme, read isr_pk back, then
TWICE STALE AS OF THE A+B MERGE (2026-08-23): K was measured against an
image with neither workstream's engine changes, and is divided by a ceiling
that now carries the dl_cache pessimism above. The 158.1% it projects for
this build is therefore NOT a load estimate and must not be reported as one.
Re-record on the next bench session before quoting any projected percentage.

_index_note: Loops are indexed by wcet.py in (body-block-count, header-address) order,
so ANY codegen change can renumber them. Each `why` below therefore names
the loop by what it IS, and the mapping was re-established from source by
building with -g and running arm-none-eabi-addr2line on each header
address (text size is identical with and without -g, so the mapping is of
the shipped code). Redo that if the count moves again; do not renumber by
eye. The default_bound of 8 covers the loops that iterate once per TAP
(NUM_TAPS) -- taps_update's 8 lanes and the specialised copies of the
8-tap read loop -- and the splice job, whose per-frame quota is capped at

0.why: splice_service()'s crossfade inner loop (engine.c). Bounded by the per-FRAME quota e->spl_quota, which engine.c caps at SPLICE_CHUNK = 8 when the job is armed (budget contract C-4). Stated explicitly rather than left to the default so that raising SPLICE_CHUNK is visible here.

1.why: Varispeed/overdub write burst `while (lp_phase >= 1.0f) { write; lp_phase -= 1; }`. lp_phase gains lp_rate per input sample and lp_rate is clamped to 4.0 in engine.c, so it can never carry more than 4 whole samples plus the sub-sample remainder: 5 iterations is the construction bound. Several specialised copies exist (plain and overdub paths, each specialised again by interpolation kernel).

10.why: The frame loop = BLOCK_FRAMES. It contains the entire per-sample engine, so it is the one loop whose bound has to be exact rather than defaulted. Was index 9 before workstream A added the dl_cache fill loop; it is the largest body in the image (457 blocks), which is the quickest way to re-identify it.

2.why: dl_cache's line fill (dc_stencil, dl_cache.h): `for (k = 0; k < DC_W; k += 4) __builtin_memcpy(&d[k], &s[k], 16)`. DC_W = 96 floats copied 4 at a time = 24 iterations, and the SDRAM reads inside it are the most expensive loads in the ISR. THIS ONE MUST BE DECLARED: its exit test is `cmp r3, ip` against a register, so infer_bound() returns None and it would silently fall back to default_bound = 8 -- a 3x undercount of the single largest burst of FMC traffic in the image. Rate-limited to one fill per lane per DC_MIN_SPAN frames, but the WCET path is allowed to assume the fill.

4.why: Pitch-shifter grain-phase wrap in ps_process (`while (phase >= len) phase -= len`). The read ratio is clamped to +/-2 octaves, so at most 4 whole grains can be crossed in one sample: 5 is the construction bound, same argument as the varispeed burst.

6.why: The negative-direction twin of loop 4 (`while (phase < 0) phase += len`), same +/-2-octave clamp, same bound. addr2line attributes it to the inlined Hermite return in delay_line.h because the wrap was scheduled into it; the instructions are a float compare-and-add cycle, not part of the polynomial.

7.why: Varispeed/overdub write burst `while (lp_phase >= 1.0f) { write; lp_phase -= 1; }`. lp_phase gains lp_rate per input sample and lp_rate is clamped to 4.0 in engine.c, so it can never carry more than 4 whole samples plus the sub-sample remainder: 5 iterations is the construction bound. Several specialised copies exist (plain and overdub paths, each specialised again by interpolation kernel). (overdub copy: body carries the write limiter.)

8.why: Varispeed/overdub write burst `while (lp_phase >= 1.0f) { write; lp_phase -= 1; }`. lp_phase gains lp_rate per input sample and lp_rate is clamped to 4.0 in engine.c, so it can never carry more than 4 whole samples plus the sub-sample remainder: 5 iterations is the construction bound. Several specialised copies exist (plain and overdub paths, each specialised again by interpolation kernel). (overdub copy: body carries the write limiter.)

dl_read_frac.why: Replaces read_frac_at_index(), which workstream A deleted. Loop-free, and worth stating explicitly: the `while (r < 0) r += len` / `while (r >= len) r -= len` normalisation loops live in dl_read_at(), the FLOAT-index read, which the audio path does not call. The exact int+frac path the engine actually uses wraps with conditional adds. If a future change routes the ISR through dl_read_at, this count changes and the build fails -- which is the point, because those loops are bounded only by a caller invariant (position within a buffer length of the range), not by construction.

dl_read_loop_frac.why: Loop-free for the same reason: the loop-window mapping is conditional arithmetic, not a normalisation loop.

ps_read_bl.why: The polyphase FIR accumulation over AA_TAPS = 16 coefficients.
